title: Implement decode() — full block with begin/end framing
description:
Implement pub fn decode(input: &[u8]) -> Result<DecodedBlock, UuError> in src/decode.rs.

DecodedBlock: { data: Vec<u8>, metadata: BlockMetadata, is_truncated: bool }
BlockMetadata: { filename: String, mode: u32 }

Algorithm:
1. Split input into lines on \n. Strip \r from each line end.
2. Find the first line starting with 'begin' (case-insensitive). If none found: Err(UuError::InvalidBeginLine).
3. If the begin line starts with 'begin-base64': Err(UuError::BeginBase64).
4. Parse begin line by splitting on ASCII whitespace (handles tabs, multiple spaces): tokens[0]='begin', tokens[1]=mode (parse as octal u32, default 0 on failure), tokens[2..]=filename (rejoin with single space to handle filenames with spaces). Strip trailing \r from filename.
5. For each subsequent line, call decode_line(). If decode_line returns Ok(0): terminator found, look for 'end' line (case-insensitive, skip blank lines), set is_truncated=false, return Ok.
6. If EOF before terminator or end: set is_truncated=true, return Ok with partial data (not Err — partial data is useful).
7. If decode_line returns Err: set is_truncated=true, return Ok with data decoded so far. Rationale: returning partial data on corruption is more useful than returning nothing.

Strict rule: no panics on any input whatsoever.

Tests (oracle: Python uu module or UNIX uuencode, NOT this crate):
- Well-formed block: correct data, metadata, is_truncated=false
- CRLF line endings throughout
- Trailing spaces stripped from data lines (shorter than length implies)
- begin-base64 -> Err(BeginBase64)
- Malformed begin line -> Err(InvalidBeginLine)
- Missing end (truncated) -> Ok with is_truncated=true
- Filename with spaces: 'begin 644 My File.doc' -> filename='My File.doc'
- Empty filename: 'begin 644 ' or 'begin 644' -> filename='' 
- Tabs in begin line: 'begin\t644\tfile.txt'
- mode with leading zero: 'begin 0644 file' -> mode=0o644=420
- Backtick and space both accepted as terminator
- Blank line accepted as terminator (space stripped by mailer)
- begin line NOT at start: input has leading garbage lines before begin
